profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI (also known as Ai2) is a nonprofit AI research laboratory founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. The organization describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering to tackle key problems in artificial intelligence, guided by open, collaborative, and inclusive principles aimed at producing safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems. The site notes partnerships with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the NSF on an open multimodal AI infrastructure project, and Google Cloud to support model development and AI platforms for scientific and environmental research.

Ai2 develops and releases AI tools oriented toward both general research and applied scientific domains. Its open-source language model, AI2 OLMo, is notable for making its full training data publicly available as part of the organization's commitment to research transparency. Semantic Scholar, its academic search product, applies AI to surface paper summaries and citation graphs for researchers. The site also describes applying AI to planetary and environmental data, with stated applications in climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife protection.

The held facts confirm Ai2 is a verified nonprofit research lab with no recorded litigation or MCP server presence in this site's registry.
